# Word paragraph capitalization and excessive probing: exact requirements review

## Verdict

**PASS for the exact source requirements review and final candidate formatting binding; no blocking finding.** Candidate `8ad780a9f733dc13f474c1227dcb1d2c5f486187` retains the approved behavior. Actual Word acceptance remains pending. No measured speed or hang-resolution claim is made.

Reviewed the active `windows_runtime_v201.rs` and exact changed native/selection/helper files against the original implementation. No implementation edits or remote actions were performed.

## Exact work files

| File relative to word-auto-task/work | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `src/windows_runtime_v201.rs` | `a41e354bf9a37ed579d4b1fe663cfd3697db6bb6a7ea8628c8a39edee5cbaaef` |
| `src/windows_runtime/selection.rs` | `1d7f3d7dbfccde5b875914a82e06f09e2f4034778532d08997ac3f52946ee0c9` |
| `src/windows_runtime/word_native.rs` | `a4f37126ce606cf0364d518210ee32d09f9f5621817179a9deed7ebb84797e63` |
| `src/windows_runtime/word_auto_correct.rs` | `4b0282280a357f0f3f5ee046e7d4c5b4b7b81fbb49cc47b5368eb55fdaf2e55c` |

## Requirement findings

- Per-key Word routing now uses only class/process identity through `selection::is_word_target`. It bypasses `has_adapter` solely at the key-event admission condition. Existing secure-input handling, UIA/password refusal and later operation availability checks remain. Mutation still enters the original native context and guards.
- `prepare_edit_suffix` branches recognized Word away from the 50-poll loop. Word preparation calls `prepare_once` with one fresh `snapshot_caret` read and returns `None` immediately on permanent mismatch. Other controls retain their prior delivery polling.
- Exact suffixes pass unchanged. Capitalization adaptation requires one lowercase first character with a single BMP uppercase counterpart, exact remaining suffix and delimiter, and an empty prefix before the word or a prefix ending in native paragraph mark `\r`. Midparagraph uppercase drift, whitespace before a paragraph word, other edits and Unicode uppercase expansion are refused. Replacement capitalization is likewise length-preserving and limited to its first character.
- Runtime updates `pending.original_text` to actual observed case and `pending.replacement_text` to actual corrected case before mutation. The corrected token is taken at its original character length, excluding the delimiter. Existing RuntimeUndo stores these resulting exact strings; context tokens and corrected-length tracking use the corrected actual token.
- Native replacement implementation is untouched. Full evolving range/document checks, fresh UIA focus/security snapshots, native document protection/structural refusal, generation/pause/document/selection identity, one-character formatting-preserving writes, custom one-Undo record, serialization and uncertain-mutation latch remain. Preparation does not bypass fresh guarded mutation, and mismatch does not trigger blind retry, clipboard or global Word flags.

## Verification and remaining evidence

Static comparison confirms the native mutation body is byte-unchanged relative to the original. The helper contains five portable tests covering document start, later paragraph/Enter/tab, exact case, arbitrary edit/delimiter/midparagraph/expansion refusal and a one-read permanent mismatch. Tests were read, not executed in this review; the parent plans hosted-worker old exact-match RED then helper GREEN before commit.

Actual Word remains necessary to verify paragraph-start correction, original-case restoration by runtime Undo, one custom Word Undo, mixed formatting, focus/protection/generation refusal and observed responsiveness. Removing repeated native probes provides a concrete reduction in interop work but does not prove latency or hang resolution. Key classification is routing, not proof that a protected or unsupported Word document is writable; operation refusal remains authoritative.

## Prior diagnosis


Runtime key-event handling calls `selection::is_standard_edit`, whose Word adapter branch invokes `word_native::has_adapter`. That opens a new joined STA, reads native document/selection and repeatedly validates UIA/focus/protection/structural state on every key event. At pending correction, the same adapter availability probe occurs again, then `wait_for_edit_suffix` performs up to 50 synchronous suffix snapshots. Each Word snapshot opens another STA and performs native and UIA checks. The nominal one-millisecond sleeps do not bound the COM work in each iteration.

The suffix comparison is exact. Typed candidate `ghbdtn ` and actual paragraph-start Word text `Ghbdtn ` therefore mismatch on all iterations. This explains a repeated-probe path directly triggered by Word capitalization; it supports a plausible cause of caret activity and blocking, but actual hangs and latency still require Word runtime observation.

The active runtime differs only in line wrapping of the key-admission condition. The helper differs only in test formatting and trailing commas; its production implementation is byte-identical. No semantics changed, so the prior requirements verdict carries to these exact candidate hashes.

The per-key Word bypass removes adapter admission COM work while retaining secure-input and UIA/password refusal before policy readiness. This was a read-only source review: no worker, tests, compilation, Word operation or remote mutation was executed.
